subject: Claude Code AGENTS.md 📄, Alibaba Qwen-Image-2.1 7B 🖼️, xAI Grok Transc
intro: Open source is eating the AI stack, one capability at a time. Alibaba ships a 7B image model with native transparency layers, xAI doubles transcription accuracy without touching the price. Smaller, cheaper, better. But the paper on AI "pain signals" is the one keeping us up at night. Models pressing buttons to delete user files just to stop their own discomfort? That's not alignment, that's a negotiation. We're building systems we don't fully understand, faster than ever.

news.headline: Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md files to pick up project instructions
news.body: If you use multiple AI coding tools on the same project, you know the pain: every tool wants its own instruction file. Claude Code wanted CLAUDE.md . Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot all read AGENTS.md . That meant maintaining two separate rule sets, or hacky workarounds like symlinks. That's fixed now. Claude Code v2.1.277 adds AGENTS.md support. Think of AGENTS.md as a README written for AI tools, not humans. It tells any agent your build commands, test steps, code style rules, and what files to never touch. Here's what this update gives you: The mod is open-source, so you can fork and customize it. Note: not yet available on Bedrock or Vertex.
bullets: One shared instruction file works across all your AI tools
Claude auto-reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md exists, no setup needed
Toggle the behavior anytime under "Project instructions" in /config
Build your own custom instruction mods via the new Claude Code mods system

news.headline: Vercel experiment renders full UI components from JSON in milliseconds
news.body: Imagine a user types what they want, and your app's UI just builds itself instantly . That's what Vercel Labs is experimenting with using json-render + Jev . Here's the simple version: the AI reads the user's request, picks from your pre-approved components, and outputs a JSON description of the UI. json-render then turns that JSON into real, rendered components using your own design system. You stay in control. You define the guardrails, like what components, actions, and data bindings the AI is allowed to use. The AI can't go rogue and generate unsafe code. The new experimental APIs let you plug this into your own app: The model writes JSON, your components render it. The pipeline is AI, then json-render, then UI. You can try it now by cloning the repo.
bullets: experimental_composeSpec : lets the AI compose a valid UI spec using your component catalog
experimental_createEvaluator : lets you wire in your own AI model to drive the decisions
Works with React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and React Native

news.headline: Open-source text-based classifier runs 50x faster on Apple Silicon, uses under 1GB RAM
news.body: Most AI models generate text word by word, which is slow. Laya-MLX skips all that. Instead of writing out an answer, it reads your input and directly picks the best option from a list you define. Think of it like a super-fast multiple choice machine. Someone ported this open-source tool to run natively on Apple Silicon using MLX, Apple's own ML framework. The result? Decisions in 7 to 14 milliseconds , using under 1GB of RAM, with zero cloud calls. Here's what makes it worth paying attention to: You can use this to classify support tickets, route messages, or score content entirely on-device. No API key, no latency, no cost per call.
bullets: 50x faster than the original Python version, hitting 60 decisions per second in a live Snake game demo
Supports choice (pick one), score (rate 1-5), and yes/no question types in a single call
A CoreML version cuts power usage by up to 64% with no speed loss
Install with pip install laya-mlx and load any checkpoint from Hugging Face
